answer.answer: No. kg never calls a language model and needs no API keys (RF-24); the benchmark is the only part that calls an LLM, and it sits outside the kg package. An external agent (Claude Code or another AI assistant) reads the documents and works out the decisions and concepts. kg's own parser (`kg extract`) only maps the code. The agent reads the guide (`kg guide`, which `kg guide --skill` exports as the kg-graph skill) and the JSON Schema (`kg schema`). It then writes a JSON draft with nodes such as Document, Decision and Concept and their edges, each with provenance method `llm`, its extractor name and a confidence. It checks the draft against the store with `kg add draft.json --dry-run --json`, fixes any errors, and merges it with `kg add`. kg supplies the schema, the guidelines, validation and merging, and a parser fact wins over an llm one when they conflict.

No. Per decision:no-embedded-llm ("No LLM inside kg", RF-24, accepted), kg never calls an LLM nor needs API keys. External agents (e.g. Claude Code, the extractor recorded on those nodes) read the documents and decisions and send kg JSON. That JSON is validated and merged into the .kg store with `kg add` (kg.merge.add_to_store, CLI kg.cli._add), merging by ID; the agent-written nodes carry provenance method "llm". The kg.agents package (kg guide / skill) gives those external agents the guidelines (RF-20). On merge, parser provenance wins over llm/manual provenance so enrichment cannot wipe deterministic data (decision:parser-wins-over-llm). Note: the graph is reported as stale relative to the code.
